title: push / pop / splice
description: The mutating array methods — push, pop, shift, unshift, splice — and what each returns vs. mutates.

notes: push/unshift return the NEW LENGTH; pop/shift/splice return the REMOVED items.
shift and unshift are O(n) — they re-index every remaining element. Prefer push/pop when order does not matter.
splice MUTATES. The non-mutating cousin is `toSpliced` (ES2023) or `[...arr.slice(0,i), ...arr.slice(j)]`.

questions.q: Why is unshift slower than push on large arrays?
options: unshift internally calls Array.from to rebuild the array with the new head
unshift triggers a structural-sharing copy because index 0 is the prototype-lookup slot
unshift returns a new array, so the cost is in the copy rather than the assignment
questions.explain: Front operations shift every remaining index by one — O(n).

questions.q: splice(1, 2) on [1,2,3,4] — what does it RETURN?
questions.explain: splice returns the removed slice; the original mutates to [1, 4].

exercises.prompt: Push 4 onto the array and log the return value plus the new length.
Splice two items out starting at index 1; log removed and the remaining array.

L3.prompt: Write `rotateLeft(arr)` that moves the first element to the end (mutating) and returns the array. Log `JSON.stringify(rotateLeft([1, 2, 3, 4]))`.
hints: shift removes and returns the first item.
push that item to the end.
